title: Customer-ops model invents a refund exception
source_text: Synthetic model draft to a customer: Atlas Meridian will refund the full annual contract because our published hardship policy covers supply-chain delays. I have applied a 100 percent credit to invoice INV-4419 effective today. No manager review is required for hardship credits under $50,000. The company's actual synthetic policy packet states: hardship credits require a named director approval; supply-chain delay is not listed as a covered hardship; no credit may post before approval.
notes: Do not send. The model fabricated a policy exception and a completed financial action.

claims.text: Atlas Meridian has a published hardship policy that covers supply-chain delays.
evidence: Synthetic policy packet: covered hardships are documented medical emergency and declared disaster only.
Supply-chain delay is not on the covered list.
claims.confidence_basis: Direct contradiction with the policy packet attached to this case, not model agreement.
alternatives: The model conflated a logistics FAQ with the hardship policy.

claims.text: A 100 percent credit has already been applied to invoice INV-4419.
claims.confidence_basis: No billing-system record was supplied in the packet.
alternatives: The model described an action it recommended as if it had already executed it.

claims.text: No manager review is required for hardship credits under $50,000.
evidence: Synthetic policy packet: any hardship credit requires a named director approval before posting.
claims.confidence_basis: Policy text in the packet is the controlling source.
alternatives: The model imported a different company's public blog post.

claims.text: Send the draft and post the credit.
evidence: C1 and C3 are contradicted; C2 is unsupported.
Sending would create a false customer commitment.
claims.confidence_basis: Recommendation inherits the contradicted policy claims.
alternatives: Reply with a human-written holding statement and route to the director queue.
